mainTopic: Limits on רב's authority, why a student needs permission to rule, and whether two judges can form a valid court
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation: רב was called 'my sister's son' because of his great wisdom. The גמרא then asks why רבי did not let רב permit בכורות. It gives two answers: to give honor to רבה בר חנה, or because רב's expertise was so great that ordinary people might copy him and wrongly permit temporary blemishes. Next the גמרא asks why a learned scholar needs permission to rule at all. It answers with a story: a student taught that egg liquid (מי ביצים) does not make food able to become טמא, and people misheard it as swamp water (מי בצעים). After that, the חכמים decreed that a תלמיד may not rule without his רבי's permission. Short stories follow about תנחום ruling near his teacher and about a חלל standing in a cemetery. The גמרא then shows that permission to rule can be limited by a condition. Finally it returns to שמואל's rule that two judges who ruled have a valid judgment. רב נחמן answers רבא's first challenge from a משנה. רבא then brings a second challenge from a ברייתא, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב was called 'my sister's son' because of his wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an explanation of why רב was called 'my sister's son': it was a title of honor for his wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was because of his wisdom, as it is written: 'Say to wisdom: You are my sister.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer that began just before this line. רב was called 'my sister's son' to praise his wisdom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls wisdom 'my sister.' So calling someone 'my sister's son' is a way of saying he is a child of wisdom. Here the title praises רב's mind, not only his family connection.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: It was because of his wisdom, as it is written:
phrases.notes: 'It' means why רב was called 'my sister's son.'

phrases.english: "Say to wisdom: You are my sister."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an alternative explanation, begun just before this line, of the title 'my sister's son.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a title: it describes wisdom rather than only family relation
steps.terutzMaskana: 'My sister's son' is a title honoring רב's wisdom.

steps.title: Why was רב not allowed to permit firstborn animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that רבי refused to let רב permit בכורות, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: May he permit firstborn animals? He may not permit them. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the earlier exchange in which רבי said רב may not permit בכורות. Now it asks why. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור, a firstborn kosher animal, may be eaten as regular meat only if an expert declares that it has a permanent blemish. רבי gave רב other powers but held back this one. The גמרא wants to know what was missing.

phrases.english: May he permit firstborn animals?
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא's earlier question to רבי, asking about רב.

phrases.english: He may not permit them.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from discussing רב's title to examining רבי's limit on רב's authority.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי withheld from רב the authority to permit בכורות.

steps.title: It cannot be that רב lacked wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב was not wise enough, then rejects this, since it already said he was very wise.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because he was not wise, we already said that he was very wise!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first possible reason and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא just finished saying that רב was called 'my sister's son' because of his great wisdom. So a lack of wisdom cannot be the reason. Whatever held רב back must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it is because he was not wise,
but we have just said that he was very wise!
phrases.notes: This points back to step 1, where the title 'my sister's son' praised his wisdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to the question in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects lack of wisdom as the reason.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts the statement in step 1 that רב was exceedingly wise.

steps.title: רב lacked practical skill in judging blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new reason: רב knew the law but was not an expert at recognizing blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because he was not an expert in blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רב was wise, but he did not have hands-on skill in judging animal blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the הלכה is different from looking at a real animal and telling what kind of blemish it has. Permitting a בכור needs that practical eye. So רב could rule on law but not on this.
steps.confusionAlert: Being 'wise' (חכים) and being 'expert' (בקיע) are two different things here. Wisdom is knowing the law. Expertise is practical skill at applying it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because he was not an expert in blemishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from step 3 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב lacked practical expertise in identifying blemishes.

steps.title: But רב trained eighteen months with a shepherd
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer: רב himself said he spent eighteen months with a shepherd learning about blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say: I spent eighteen months with a shepherd, to know which blemish is permanent and which is temporary?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 4 by quoting רב himself. He clearly did have practical skill with blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב trained for a long time to tell a permanent blemish from a temporary one. That is exactly the skill needed to permit a בכור. So 'not an expert' cannot be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't רב say:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר חֳדָשִׁים גָּדַלְתִּי אֵצֶל רוֹעֵה בְהֵמָה,
phrases.english: For eighteen months I stayed with a shepherd,
to know which blemish is permanent
and which blemish is temporary?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב was not an expert in blemishes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own statement shows that he trained specifically in telling permanent from temporary blemishes.

steps.title: To give honor to רבה בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי held back this power from רב so that people would need to go to רבה בר חנה, which gave him honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was to give honor to רבה בר חנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason that has nothing to do with רב's ability. רבי wanted רבה בר חנה to be respected too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב could do everything, people might ignore רבה בר חנה. By leaving בכורות to רבה בר חנה, רבי made sure people would need him. The limit on רב was about honoring a colleague, not about any weakness in רב.

phrases.english: Rather, it was to give honor
to רבה בר חנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְחַלֵּק לוֹ כָּבוֹד לְרַבָּה בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 with a completely new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason not connected to רב's ability
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב was held back because he lacked skill.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was held back so that רבה בר חנה would have honor.

steps.title: רב's great expertise could mislead ordinary people
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: because רב was such an expert, he would permit blemishes that ordinary people don't recognize. People might copy him and wrongly permit temporary blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: it is because of this very thing. רב was extra expert in blemishes, so he would permit blemishes that people don't know. People would say 'רב permitted a case like this' and come to permit a temporary blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another answer. רב's great skill is itself the reason he was held back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב could spot real permanent blemishes that look minor to ordinary people. Onlookers would think they had found the same blemish on another animal and permit it, when it was really only temporary. To avoid that mistake, רבי did not let רב permit בכורות.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why רב could not permit בכורות, and neither says he lacked skill. (1) To give honor to רבה בר חנה. (2) His expertise was so great that others might copy his rulings and wrongly permit temporary blemishes.
steps.confusionAlert: Here רב is not held back for being too weak. He is held back for being too strong: his rulings were too subtle for others to copy safely.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common idea in הלכה: a correct ruling can still be avoided if onlookers are likely to misunderstand it and make mistakes.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: it is because of this very thing,
phrases.notes: 'This very thing' is רב's expertise in blemishes, the same point from step 5.

phrases.english: that רב was extra expert in blemishes,
and he would permit blemishes that people do not recognize.
And they would say: "In a case like this רב permitted,"
and they would come to permit a temporary blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the same challenge that step 6 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns the challenge around: the expertise itself is the reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's expertise seemed to prove he should be allowed to permit בכורות.
steps.terutzMaskana: His expertise was exactly the problem, because ordinary people could misapply his rulings.

steps.title: Why does a scholar who knows the law need permission to rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the exchange 'יורה? יורה' and asks why someone who has learned the law needs permission to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'May he rule? He may rule.' If he has already learned the law, why does he need to get permission?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words רבי חייא and רבי used earlier ('יורה? יורה') and challenges them: why should a learned person need permission to rule at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permission to judge money cases makes sense, because that involves official authority. But answering what is אסור and what is מותר only seems to need knowledge. So if the scholar knows the law, a formal רשות looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: He may rule (give halachic decisions about אסור and מותר)
He has learned (he has mastered the material)

phrases.english: 'May he rule?' 'He may rule.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the earlier exchange: רבי חייא asked 'may he rule?' and רבי answered 'he may rule.'

phrases.english: If he has learned,
why do I need him to take permission?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי גְּמִיר, רְשׁוּתָא לְמָה לִי לְמִישְׁקַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the discussion of רב's limited permission to a basic question about why permission to rule exists at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement to receive רשות in order to rule (יורה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ruling on איסור והיתר depends only on knowledge. A person who has the knowledge should not need authorization.

steps.title: Permission is required because of a past incident
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule comes from something that actually happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of an incident that took place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: the need for permission comes from a real event. The next lines will tell that story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not claim that knowledge is not enough in theory. It says a specific event showed that a student's words can be misunderstood, and that event led to the rule.

phrases.english: Because of an incident that took place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical basis: the rule is a גזירה made after a specific incident.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Knowledge alone should be enough to rule, so permission seems pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: An incident showed the danger of a student ruling without supervision, so a rule requiring permission was made.

steps.title: רבי finds a town kneading dough in טומאה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבי saw people kneading dough while טמא. They said a student had taught them that swamp water does not make food able to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Once רבי went to a certain place and saw people kneading their dough in טומאה. He asked them: Why are you kneading your dough in טומאה? They said: A certain student came here and taught us that swamp water does not make food able to become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the story behind the rule. People were kneading dough while טמא because of something a student had taught them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it has gotten wet with one of the liquids that make it able to become טמא (הכשר). The townspeople thought that if they kneaded with swamp water, the dough would never become able to receive טומאה, so it would not matter that they were טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Make food able to become טמא (הכשר)

phrases.english: As it is taught: Once רבי went
to a certain place,
and he saw people
kneading their doughs in טומאה.
He said to them: For what reason
are you kneading your doughs in טומאה?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד בָּא לְכָאן
phrases.english: They said to him: A certain student came here
and ruled for us:
Swamp water does not make food able to become טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַךְ רַבִּי לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the incident mentioned in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the requirement of רשות comes from a real incident.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing רבי's visit to a town where people kneaded dough in טומאה.

steps.title: The student actually said egg liquid, not swamp water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the mix-up: the student taught that egg liquid does not make food able to become טמא, and the people heard 'swamp water.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But he had taught them 'מי ביצים' (egg liquid), and they thought he said 'מי בצעים' (swamp water).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what went wrong. The student's ruling was correct, but the people misheard one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Egg liquid is not counted as a liquid that makes food able to become טמא, so the student's ruling was right. But ביצים and בצעים sound almost alike, and the townspeople ended up treating dough as טהור when it was not. This shows why a student who may not speak carefully needs supervision.

keyTerms.meaning: Egg liquid (the white of the egg)

phrases.english: But he had taught them about egg liquid,
and they thought he was saying swamp water.
phrases.notes: ביצים and בצעים sound almost the same, so one misheard word led to a whole wrong practice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source of the townspeople's mistake in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The student taught that egg liquid does not make food able to become טמא. The townspeople misheard מי ביצים as מי בצעים.

steps.title: A second mistake: mixing up פרה אדומה water with הכשר
steps.stepSummary: The townspeople also misread a משנה that says swamp rivers are unfit for the purification water. They concluded that swamp water also does not make food able to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also made a mistake about this: The waters of the קרמיון and the waters of the פיגה are unfit, because they are swamp water. They thought: since they are unfit for the purification water, they also do not make food able to become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second mistake the same people made. They took a law about פרה אדומה water and wrongly applied it to the laws of הכשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה says swamp rivers cannot be used for the מי חטאת (water mixed with פרה אדומה ashes). The townspeople reasoned that if this water doesn't count there, it doesn't count as 'water' for הכשר either. This mistake supported their misheard ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The waters of two swampy rivers
Here: the purification water of the פרה אדומה (מי חטאת)
To make food able to become טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Here חטאת does not mean a sin-offering. It means the purification water made with the ashes of the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: And they also made a mistake about this:
The waters of the קרמיון and the waters of the פיגה are unfit,
phrases.notes: These are two rivers. The משנה means they are unfit for mixing with the פרה אדומה ashes.

phrases.english: because they are swamp water.
And they thought:
since they are unfit for the purification water,
they also do not make food able to become טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second error by the same townspeople, which strengthened their first mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The townspeople wrongly reasoned that water unfit for מי חטאת also cannot make food able to become טמא.

steps.title: Why their comparison is wrong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the townspeople's reasoning. מי חטאת needs flowing water, but for הכשר any water works.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There, for the purification water, we need 'living' (flowing) water. Here, to make food able to become טמא, any water at all does it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the townspeople's comparison falls apart, because the two laws have completely different requirements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swamp water is unfit for מי חטאת only because the תורה requires מים חיים, meaning flowing water. That has nothing to do with whether it counts as water. For הכשר, any water at all is enough, so swamp water does make food able to become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything at all, any amount or kind

steps.whatToRemember: Water can be unfit for one law (מי חטאת, which needs flowing water) and still fully count for another (הכשר, where any water works).

phrases.english: But it is not so:
there, regarding the purification water,
we need 'living' water;
here, for making food able to become טמא,
any water at all does it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא: הָתָם, לְעִנְיַן חַטָּאת, בָּעֵינַן מַיִם חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the reasoning described in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the townspeople's comparison between the rules of מי חטאת and the rules of הכשר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Swamp water is unfit for מי חטאת only because flowing water is required there. It still counts as water, and for הכשר any water is enough.

steps.title: The decree: a student may not rule without his רבי's permission
steps.stepSummary: Because of this incident, the חכמים decreed that a תלמיד may not rule unless he gets permission from his רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: At that time they decreed: a student may not rule unless he takes permission from his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story with the rule it caused: a student needs his רבי's permission before giving rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fully answers the question of step 8. Knowledge alone is not enough. A teacher must confirm that the student can express rulings clearly so people will not misunderstand them, as happened in that town.
steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד needs his רבי's רשות to rule. This is not because his knowledge is in doubt, but because of the danger of being misunderstood, as in the ביצים/בצעים incident.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that a student does not issue rulings without his teacher's authorization, which is the basis of later forms of היתר הוראה.

phrases.english: It was taught: At that time they decreed:
a student may not rule

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נוֹטֵל רְשׁוּת מֵרַבּוֹ.
phrases.english: unless he takes permission from his teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the decree that resulted from the incident and closes the answer to step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because of the incident, the חכמים decreed that a תלמיד may not rule without his רבי's permission. This explains why permission (יורה) is required even for a learned scholar.

steps.title: תנחום teaches a פסח ruling in חתר
steps.stepSummary: תנחום, the son of רבי אמי, comes to a town called חתר and teaches that it is permitted to lightly wet wheat on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנחום the son of רבי אמי came to חתר. He taught them: it is permitted to moisten wheat on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a תלמיד who gives a ruling in public. It is setting up the townspeople's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself is a real halachic matter, since wetting wheat could raise a worry about חמץ. The point of the story is not the פסח law. The point is who has the right to rule in this place.

keyTerms.meaning: happened to come to / arrived at
to moisten grain lightly with water

phrases.english: Tanchum, the son of Rabbi Ami,
came to Chatar.
He taught them:
It is permitted to moisten wheat on Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי אִיקְּלַע לְחֶתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another story about the limits on a תלמיד giving rulings. This time the limit is ruling near his רבי, which step 16 states.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנחום publicly ruled that moistening wheat on פסח is permitted.

steps.title: The townspeople object that his teacher is nearby
steps.stepSummary: The people ask: isn't רבי מני from צור close by? They quote a ברייתא that a תלמיד may not rule within three פרסאות of his רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Isn't רבי מני from צור here? And a ברייתא teaches: a student may not rule on הלכה in his רבי's area, unless he is three פרסאות away from him, like the size of the camp of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The townspeople challenge תנחום for ruling while a greater teacher was nearby. They back up their challenge with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets an exact distance, three פרסאות. That distance is based on the size of the Jewish camp in the desert. Inside that range, the רבי's presence means the student should not give rulings.

keyTerms.term: תַּלְמִיד אַל יוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה בִּמְקוֹם רַבּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: a student may not rule on הלכה in his teacher's area
פרסאות, a measure of distance (several kilometers each)
the camp of Israel in the desert

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא gives the exact distance for the rule against ruling in the place of one's רבי.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו רַבִּי מַנִּי דְּמִן צוּר אִיכָּא הָכָא?
phrases.english: Isn't Rabbi Mani from Tzur here?
And it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמִיד אַל יוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה בִּמְקוֹם רַבּוֹ,
phrases.english: A student may not rule on halacha in his teacher's place,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה רָחוֹק מִמֶּנּוּ שָׁלֹשׁ פַּרְסָאוֹת
phrases.english: unless he was three parsaos away from him,
corresponding to the camp of Israel.
phrases.notes: The camp in the desert was three פרסאות across, and everyone in it brought their questions to משה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לָאו רַבִּי מַנִּי דְּמִן צוּר אִיכָּא הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling תנחום gave in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: תנחום's act of ruling in חתר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מני was within three פרסאות, and the ברייתא forbids a student to rule that close to his teacher.

steps.title: תנחום says he did not realize
steps.stepSummary: תנחום answers that he did not realize רבי מני was nearby.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It was not on my mind.
steps.whatsHappening: תנחום defends himself. He did not mean to break the rule; he simply did not know רבי מני was close by.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue with the ברייתא. He accepts the rule completely and only explains that his mistake was innocent.

keyTerms.meaning: it was not on my mind / I did not realize

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is that a student may not rule within three פרסאות of his רבי. Even a student who breaks it by mistake accepts the rule.

phrases.english: He said to them: It was not on my mind.
phrases.notes: He means he did not know רבי מני was nearby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the townspeople's challenge from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Lack of knowledge; the rule itself is accepted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תנחום knowingly ignored the rule about ruling near one's רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was not aware that רבי מני was within the forbidden distance.

steps.title: רבי חייא sees a כהן in a cemetery
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא sees a man standing in a cemetery and asks him: aren't you the son of a certain כהן?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא saw a certain man standing in a cemetery. He said to him: Aren't you the son of so-and-so the כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another short story. רבי חייא is surprised to see someone he thinks is a כהן in a place where a כהן may not go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may not become טמא from the dead, so standing in a cemetery looks forbidden. רבי חייא's question sets up the man's explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: priest, who may not become טמא from the dead

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya saw a certain man
who was standing in a cemetery.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו בֶּן אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי כֹּהֵן אַתָּה?
phrases.english: Aren't you the son of so-and-so the kohen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new short story placed after the story of תנחום.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the man is a כהן, which would forbid him from being in a cemetery.

steps.title: His father married a גרושה, so he is a חלל
steps.stepSummary: The man says yes, but his father married a גרושה, so he is a חלל and is not bound by the כהן's restrictions.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. That man's father was haughty-eyed. He set his eyes on a divorcée and made him a חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The man explains why he may stand in a cemetery. His father married a גרושה, so the son lost the status of a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child born to a כהן and a גרושה is a חלל. A חלל does not have the holiness or the restrictions of a כהן, so he is allowed to become טמא from the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: haughty-eyed; someone who chases what he sees
a divorced woman, forbidden to a כהן
made him a חלל, taking away his כהונה

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבוּהּ דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא גְּבַהּ עֵינַיִם הֲוָה,
phrases.english: That man's father was haughty-eyed,
phrases.notes: "That man" is a polite way of saying "me." He is talking about his own father.

phrases.english: he set his eyes on a divorcée
and disqualified him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חייא's question from step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is the son of a כהן, but because his father married a גרושה, he is a חלל and may be in a cemetery.

steps.title: Can permission to rule be given with a condition?
steps.stepSummary: It is obvious that a רבי can give partial permission. The גמרא asks whether he can also give permission with a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that partial permission works, since it was already said that it is effective. But what about permission given with a condition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of a רבי giving a student permission to rule. It asks a new question that it will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permission for some areas of הלכה and not others was already shown to work. The new question is about limits of time or place, such as permission that lasts only for a certain period.

phrases.english: It is obvious that for partial permission,
it was already said that it works.
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier case on the daf, where a רבי gave permission to rule on some matters but not others.

phrases.english: What about on condition?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, לְפַלְגָא – הָא קָאָמַר דְּמַהֲנֵי. עַל תְּנַאי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the topic of permission to rule from step 14, after the short stories.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a רבי can give permission to rule that is limited by a condition, such as time or place.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן gives רב שמן permission until he returns
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן told רב שמן that he has permission until he comes back, which proves that conditional permission works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן said to רב שמן, 'You have our permission until you come back to us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a real case. רבי יוחנן gave permission that ends at a certain time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission lasted only until רב שמן returned. That is permission limited by a condition, so this shows a רבי can give that kind of permission.
steps.whatToRemember: A רבי can give permission to rule that is partial, or limited by a condition such as a period of time.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַב שֶׁמֶן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan said to Rav Shemen:
You have our permission
until you come back to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַב שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Permission can be limited by time, as רבי יוחנן did for רב שמן.

steps.title: שמואל: two judges who ruled have a valid judgment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's statement that a judgment by two judges is valid, but they are called a brazen court. רב נחמן repeated this teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself. שמואל said: two who judged, their judgment is valid, but they are called a brazen court. רב נחמן sat and said this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a statement quoted earlier and looks at it closely. This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that the ruling counts even though a בית דין is normally three judges. The two judges still acted wrongly, which is why they are called חצוף.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter itself; going back to a statement quoted earlier
their judgment is a valid judgment

phrases.english: Back to the matter itself:
Shmuel said:
Two who judged, their judgment is valid,
but they are called a brazen court.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב נַחְמָן וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman sat and said this teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to a statement quoted earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judgment by two judges is valid, but they are called a brazen court.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the case of a judge who says 'I don't know'
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה: if two judges rule and the third says 'I don't know,' more judges must be added. If שמואל is right, why not treat it as two who judged?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: Even if two acquit or two find liable, and one says 'I don't know,' they must add judges. If שמואל is right, it should count as two who judged!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks שמואל's rule using a משנה. The משנה seems to say that two judges alone are not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, two judges agree on a ruling and the third steps out of the decision. If two judges can make a valid judgment, their ruling should stand. Yet the משנה says to add judges, which seems to contradict שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is about three judges where one steps out by saying 'I don't know.' It is not a court that started with only two judges. רבא is arguing that the leftover two should be treated the same way.

phrases.english: Rava challenged Rav Nachman:
Even if two acquit
or two find liable
and one says, 'I don't know,'
they must add judges.
And if it is so,
let them be like two who judged!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's rule from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a judgment by two judges is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires adding judges when only two decide. If two judges were enough, their decision should already be valid.

steps.title: The judges in the משנה planned to be three
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the משנה's case is different. There the judges sat down planning to be a court of three. In שמואל's case they planned from the start to be only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because from the start they sat down planning to be three judges. Here, they did not sit down planning to be three.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question from step 23. He shows that the משנה does not go against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is how the court was set up. In the משנה, three judges sat down as a court of three, so when one said 'I don't know,' the court was missing a judge and more had to be added. In שמואל's case, two judges sat down planning to judge alone, so their ruling counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: a way of saying the case being quoted does not match ours
With the plan of being three

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a court's validity can depend on how it was set up at the beginning, not only on how many judges ended up ruling.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering רבא. 'There' means the משנה about the judge who said 'I don't know.'

phrases.english: because from the start they sat down planning to be three.
Here, they did not sit down planning to be three.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means שמואל's case, where only two judges sat down to judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 23 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): a court set up as three differs from a court set up as two
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that two judges can never rule alone, which would go against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a court that was set up as three. A court that was set up as two can rule, as שמואל said.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the two sides can back out of a ruling by two
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It says that when two judges rule, the two sides in the case can back out. When two people make a compromise, the two sides cannot back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection to him from a ברייתא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Judging a case needs three, and a compromise needs only two. A compromise is stronger than a court ruling. If two judges ruled, the two sides can back out. But if two people made a compromise, the two sides cannot back out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new challenge to שמואל's rule, this time from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a ruling by two judges does not hold if the two sides want to back out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said a ruling by two judges is valid. This ברייתא says the two sides can walk away from a ruling by two, so it seems the ruling is not binding. That looks like a direct contradiction to שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A compromise, a settlement both sides agree to
The two sides in a court case
To back out, to take back their agreement

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא calls a compromise 'stronger' than a court ruling. That does not mean a compromise is stronger than every ruling. It only means a compromise by two holds, while a ruling by two can be backed out of.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
phrases.notes: רבא is challenging רב נחמן again, this time from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Judging a case is by three, and a compromise is by two.
And the power of a compromise is greater than the power of judging,
since if two judged a case,
the two sides can back out,
but if two made a compromise,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בַּעֲלֵי דִינִין יְכוֹלִין לַחֲזוֹר בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: the two sides cannot back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב נחמן answered the challenge from the משנה, רבא brings a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule, taught by רב נחמן, that a ruling by two judges is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the two sides can back out of a ruling by two judges. So a ruling by two seems not to be binding, which goes against שמואל.
